world_art_prompt.scene: Key art of the fantasy world 'Postnikov Spire' at night: a colossal stone tower rising from the sea into the clouds, each floor a different room that seems to unfold into more dimensions (cube-shaped rooms opening into nested cubes, spheres wrapping spheres, a ring of interlinked glowing circles like the Hopf fibration around one floor). A spiral ascent road, 'Freudenthal Ascent', winds up the lower floors. At the very top, a violet crown-shaped structure glows ominously. A single small Gyroid (only one hero in the scene) climbs the ascent road with a gold lasso. Small violet guardians on the ledges. The stone walls are plain, with no carved writing or inscriptions.

art.prompt: A colossal tower whose floors unfold into higher dimensions, a Hopf ring of linked circles around one floor, the Freudenthal Ascent spiral road, the violet Null Crown at the top; Gyroid and Emmy climbing.

map.note: World 4 overworld layout (map units). The Spire is drawn as a side view: y is height. Sites are floors; paths are stairs; gates need earlier tools.

sites.name: Spire Foot
sites.note: Where the Reach's seam ends at the Spire's base.

gate.note: A shaft with no stair: the Sling's Freudenthal upgrade lifts Gyroid a whole dimension.
The Crown's door has one lock per world: Spool, Winding Cord, Boundary Blade, Cup Caster and the Sling.

4-1.site: Cube Hall — the Spire's first floor: a hall of cubes whose faces all fold onto one point.
4-1.story: Loops were maps of an interval with both ends at the beacon. Now: maps of a cube with its whole surface at the beacon. These are the higher homotopy groups. In two or more dimensions, there's room to slide one cube past another — so order no longer matters.
4-1.objective: Combine cube-maps and show that higher homotopy groups are abelian.
mechanics: Cube maps: an n-cube whose entire boundary is pinned to the basepoint (an element of πₙ).
Stack: glue two cubes side by side along one direction (the group operation).
Slide: shrink each into a small subcube, slide them around each other in the second direction, and regrow — f + g slides into g + f.
Contrast: in one dimension (World 1) there's no room to pass, which is why the Commutator's word mattered.
4-1.math_check: πₙ(X, x₀) as homotopy classes of maps (Iⁿ, ∂Iⁿ) → (X, x₀); πₙ is abelian for n ≥ 2 (Hatcher pp. 339–346).

stages.name: Pinned Cubes
stages.description: A square with its whole edge at the beacon is a map of a sphere.

stages.name: Stack
stages.description: Stack squares left-to-right; undo with a reversed square.

stages.name: Pass Each Other
stages.description: Shrink, slide past, regrow: order doesn't matter in two dimensions.

stages.name: One Dimension Down
stages.description: Try the same slide on intervals and fail — revisit the Commutator's patrol.

enemies.name: Cube sentry
enemies.description: New: a violet cube that pins Gyroid's boundary; lash each face (six lashes, or fewer once faces are pinned together).

enemies.name: Ribbon patrol
enemies.description: From World 1: its word cancels up here.

4-1.tools: Uses the Loop Lash (upgraded to square maps) and the Tide Glass.
4-1.music: Postnikov Spire theme: a solemn 72 bpm piece in C minor, pipe-organ chords building up a floor at a time — first statement.
4-1.visuals: A stone hall filled with cubes whose faces glow and fold toward a single gold point; two small glowing subcubes sliding past each other.

4-2.site: Grid Gallery — a gallery where everything snaps to its cell grid.
4-2.story: Any map between cell-built places can be slid to respect the cells: the k-dimensional part lands in the k-dimensional skeleton. So small spheres can't wrap big ones: πᵢ(Sⁿ) = 0 for i < n.
4-2.objective: Snap maps to cells and show small spheres slip off big spheres.
mechanics: Snap: slide a map so each k-cell lands in the k-skeleton.
Sphere test: a circle on a 2-sphere snaps into the 0-skeleton — a point — so it shrinks.
CW approximation: replace a strange place by a cell-built one with the same homotopy groups.
4-2.math_check: Cellular approximation theorem; πᵢ(Sⁿ) = 0 for i < n; CW approximation (Hatcher pp. 348–356).

stages.name: Snap
stages.description: Snap a path to a graph's edges.

stages.name: Slip Off
stages.description: A circle on a sphere snaps to a point.

stages.name: Too Small to Wrap
stages.description: Any 2-sphere on a 3-sphere slips off.

stages.name: Approximate
stages.description: Build a cell model of a strange gallery piece.

enemies.name: Glitch
enemies.description: New: a violet static sprite that knocks maps off the grid; one lash.

4-2.music: Spire theme on a grid-stepped arpeggio.
4-2.visuals: A gallery with glowing grid lines on every surface; a gold map snapping onto the grid; a circle slipping off a sphere.

4-3.site: The Weak Spot — a floor where two rooms agree on every homotopy group.
4-3.story: If a map between cell-built places matches all homotopy groups, it is a full equivalence (0-3 Mirror Couriers return). But beware: matching groups abstractly isn't enough — the map must induce them.
4-3.objective: Use Whitehead's theorem — and learn what it does not say.
mechanics: Equivalence test: a map that induces isomorphisms on every πₙ between CW complexes is a homotopy equivalence — the Mirror Couriers can be built.
Fake twins: two places with isomorphic groups but no map inducing them (S² × RP³ vs RP² × S³) — not covered by the theorem.
4-3.math_check: Whitehead's theorem; the need for a map inducing the isomorphisms (Hatcher pp. 346–348, example p. 348).

stages.name: A Map That Matches
stages.description: Check groups under a map; build the couriers.

stages.name: Weakly Equal
stages.description: Upgrade weak equivalences to equivalences.

stages.name: No Map
stages.description: Two rooms, same groups, no matching map.

stages.name: Spot the Weakness
stages.description: Sort pairs into equivalent and not proven.

4-3.music: Spire theme in a hesitant rubato.
4-3.visuals: Two identical-looking rooms facing each other across a floor, gold couriers running between them.

4-4.site: Sling Landing — a balcony at the top of the Ascent, open to a vertical shaft.
4-4.story: Suspending (0-5) shifts homotopy groups up one dimension, and in a range it changes nothing (Freudenthal). The Sling gets its upgrade: lift a whole map up a dimension. And πₙ(Sⁿ) is ℤ, counted by degree (2-6).
4-4.objective: Suspend maps up the shaft and compute πₙ(Sⁿ).
mechanics: Freudenthal Sling (upgrade of the 0-5 Suspension Sling): suspend a map of spheres; it climbs the shaft.
Stable range: πᵢ(Sⁿ) → πᵢ₊₁(Sⁿ⁺¹) is an isomorphism for i < 2n − 1 and onto for i = 2n − 1.
Degree Dial: maps Sⁿ → Sⁿ are classified by degree.
4-4.math_check: Homotopy excision, the Freudenthal suspension theorem, πₙ(Sⁿ) ≅ ℤ via degree (Hatcher pp. 360–366).

stages.name: Up One
stages.description: Suspend a circle map into a sphere map.

stages.name: Degree Is All
stages.description: Classify sphere maps by the Dial.

stages.name: The Stable Range
stages.description: Suspension stops changing anything past the range.

stages.name: Climb the Shaft
stages.description: Sling up the shaft dimension by dimension.

4-4.music: Spire theme, modulating up a step with each suspension.
4-4.visuals: A balcony over a vast vertical shaft; Gyroid slung upward on a gold double-cone of light; spheres stacked up the shaft.

4-5.site: One-Group Floors — floors with exactly one nonzero homotopy group each.
4-5.story: The One-Group Tower from World 1 had loops only. These floors generalize it: one group, in one dimension n — the Eilenberg–MacLane spaces K(G, n), the building blocks of the Spire.
4-5.objective: Build K(G, n) floors by attaching cells to kill higher groups.
mechanics: Start with a bouquet of n-spheres; attach (n+1)-cells for relations.
Kill: attach higher cells to fill every higher group, floor by floor.
4-5.math_check: Existence and uniqueness of K(G, n) CW complexes (Hatcher pp. 365–366).

stages.name: Recall
stages.description: Revisit the K(G,1) floors.

stages.name: Kill Above
stages.description: Build K(ℤ, 2) by killing higher groups of S²: an endless climb (CP^∞).

4-5.music: Music-box Sheetwater theme from World 1, now on organ.
4-5.visuals: Stacked floors each lit by a single color; Gyroid attaching glowing cells to fill openings above.

4-6.site: Hurewicz Hall — a hall where homotopy and homology meters stand side by side.
4-6.story: The first nonzero homotopy group equals the first nonzero homology group (World 2) — and in dimension one, homology is π₁ made abelian (2-10).
4-6.objective: Use the Hurewicz map to read homotopy from homology.
mechanics: Hurewicz needle: send a sphere map to the homology class of its image.
If all lower groups vanish, the needle is an isomorphism in the first nonzero dimension.
4-6.math_check: The Hurewicz theorem: for (n−1)-connected X with n ≥ 2, πₙ(X) ≅ Hₙ(X); for n = 1, abelianization (Hatcher pp. 366–375).

stages.name: Two Meters
stages.description: Compare π and H on a sphere.

stages.name: First Nonzero
stages.description: Read πₙ from Hₙ for connected places.

stages.name: Dimension One
stages.description: Revisit the Abelian Ford: H₁ = π₁ abelianized.

stages.name: Beyond the First
stages.description: Show the needle can fail above the first nonzero group.

enemies.name: Ribbon patrol
enemies.description: Dissolves in dimension one, as in 2-10.

4-6.tools: Uses the Degree Dial and Boundary Blade.
4-6.music: Spire theme with the Chain Delta theme as a countermelody.
4-6.visuals: A hall with two great meters, a brass dial and a glowing abacus, joined by a gold needle.

4-7.site: The Hopf Ring — a floor encircled by a ring of interlinked glowing circles: every circle links every other.
4-7.story: Null's World 3 claim: every map S³ → S² is trivial. The Hopf Ring refutes it. The 3-sphere is a bundle of circles over the 2-sphere, every pair linked. Its long exact sequence shows π₃(S²) = ℤ, and the Hopf map is its generator.
4-7.objective: Refute Null's World 3 claim with the Hopf fibration.
mechanics: Fiber walk: each point of a small sphere island has a whole circle above it in the Ring; any two circles link.
Bundle sequence: the circle, the 3-sphere and the 2-sphere link into a long exact sequence of homotopy groups.
Since π₃(S¹) and π₂(S¹) vanish, π₃(S³) ≅ π₃(S²): the Hopf map counts as 1 — it is not trivial.
4-7.math_check: Fiber bundles, the long exact sequence of homotopy groups, the Hopf fibration S¹ → S³ → S², π₃(S²) ≅ ℤ (Hatcher pp. 375–384). Refutes the World 3 claim.

stages.name: A Circle per Point
stages.description: Walk the sphere; watch circles above each point.

stages.name: Linked
stages.description: Any two circles link once.

stages.name: The Sequence
stages.description: Run the bundle sequence to π₃(S²) ≅ ℤ.

stages.name: Null's Answer
stages.description: Present the Hopf map; Null's claim breaks.

enemies.name: Fiber wraith
enemies.description: New: a violet wraith that slips between fibers; lash it on its own circle.

4-7.tools: Uses the Sheet Compass (fibers generalize sheets) and the Degree Dial.
4-7.music: Spire theme as a circular canon in which every voice is linked to every other.
4-7.visuals: A floor encircled by glowing gold interlinked circles arranged like the Hopf fibration, a small sphere island beneath.

4-8.site: Stable Ground — a terrace far up the Spire where suspension no longer changes anything.
4-8.story: Suspend enough times and homotopy groups of spheres settle down: the stable stems. Gyroid charts the first few.
mechanics: Stability: keep slinging until groups stop changing (from 4-4).
The first stems: ℤ, ℤ₂, ℤ₂, ℤ₂₄ — given by the book's table; the game shows them rather than computing all of them.
4-8.math_check: Stable homotopy groups πₖˢ; the first values from Hatcher's table (pp. 384–392). Flag: the game does not compute stems beyond what the text explains.

stages.name: Settle
stages.description: Watch π₄(S³), π₅(S⁴)… settle.

stages.name: The Table
stages.description: Fill a chart of stable stems from the book's table.

4-8.music: Spire theme over a steady pedal note that never changes.
4-8.visuals: A calm stone terrace above the clouds; a chart carved into a wall (no text) of glowing beads.

4-9.site: The Classing Room — a room where readings (World 3) become maps into the One-Group Floors.
4-9.story: A cohomology class is the same as a map into a K(G, n) floor, up to sliding. Readings are maps.
4-9.objective: Turn readings into maps and back.
mechanics: Pull-back: map a place into K(G, n) and pull back the floor's fundamental reading.
Every reading arises this way, uniquely up to homotopy.
4-9.math_check: Hⁿ(X; G) ≅ ⟨X, K(G, n)⟩ for CW complexes (Hatcher pp. 393–405).

stages.name: Pull Back
stages.description: Map a circle into K(ℤ,1) = S¹; get its reading.

stages.name: Readings Are Maps
stages.description: Turn a torus reading into a map and back.

4-9.music: Gardens theme from World 3 in the Spire's organ registration.
4-9.visuals: A room where lantern beams (World 3) bend into gold rails leading up to a single-color floor above.

4-10.site: Fibration Station — a station where every track lifts: the homotopy lifting property, for any path and any deformation.
4-10.story: Covers (World 1) lifted paths. Fibrations lift every deformation — and give long exact sequences. Any map can be turned into one.
4-10.objective: Lift deformations through fibrations and use their exact sequence.
mechanics: Lift: given a deformation below and a start above, the station builds the lift (homotopy lifting).
Path fibration: turn any map into a fibration by adding path tracks.
Loop space: the fiber of the path fibration is the loop space.
4-10.math_check: Fibrations, the homotopy lifting property, the long exact sequence, path-space fibrations and loop spaces (Hatcher pp. 405–410).

stages.name: Lift
stages.description: Lift deformations through a product.

stages.name: Make It Fibre
stages.description: Convert a map into a fibration.

stages.name: The Loop Space
stages.description: Find the fiber of the path fibration.

4-10.music: The Sheetwater theme from World 1 re-scored for the Spire.
4-10.visuals: A station of layered tracks, trains on upper tracks shadowing every move on the lower tracks.

4-11.site: The Twist — a floor where the Spire's stages are joined by twisted brackets.
4-11.story: Every place is built as a tower of One-Group Floors joined by twists — the k-invariants. Null's final claim is that the twists don't matter. Here Gyroid sees that the same floors with different twists make different places.
4-11.objective: Build Postnikov towers and see that k-invariants change the space.
mechanics: Tower: stack stages Xₙ, each obtained from the one below with a K(πₙ, n) fiber.
Twist bracket: each stage is attached by a k-invariant (a cohomology class, 4-9).

Same groups, different twists: a two-stage tower with groups G (dimension m) and H (dimension n) is the product K(G,m) × K(H,n) when its k-invariant is zero, and a different, twisted place when it isn't.
4-11.math_check: Postnikov towers and k-invariants; spaces with the same homotopy groups can differ (Hatcher pp. 410–415).

stages.name: Stack the Floors
stages.description: Build a two-stage tower.

stages.name: The Twist
stages.description: Read each stage's k-invariant.

stages.name: Untwisted
stages.description: Untwist it and get a different place.

stages.name: Rebuild
stages.description: Rebuild a damaged tower with its k-invariants.

enemies.name: Twist thief
enemies.description: New: a violet hand that steals brackets; two lashes.

4-11.tools: Uses the Cup Caster and Cell-Smith.
4-11.music: Spire theme with a dissonant twist chord between stages.
4-11.visuals: Stacked floors of the Spire joined by twisted glowing gold brackets; violet hands prying at them.

4-12.site: Obstruction Course — the last floor before the Crown: extend a map cell by cell, climbing as you go.
4-12.story: Extending a map over a cell-built place, one cell at a time: each step either succeeds or meets an obstruction — a cohomology class. The Extension Cord from World 0 (0-B) returns at full power.
4-12.objective: Extend maps cell by cell and read the obstructions.
mechanics: Climb: extend a map over the k-skeleton, then try each (k+1)-cell.
Obstruction: the map on a cell's boundary gives an element of πₖ; together they form a cohomology class.
Zero class: change the map on lower cells and continue.
4-12.math_check: Obstruction theory for extending maps; obstruction classes in Hᵏ⁺¹(X; πₖ(Y)) (Hatcher pp. 415–420).

stages.name: Cell by Cell
stages.description: Extend a map over a disk's cells.

stages.name: Blocked
stages.description: A cell whose boundary wraps a sphere nontrivially blocks the climb.

stages.name: Reroute
stages.description: When the class is zero, change lower choices and continue.

stages.name: The Summit
stages.description: Climb to the Crown's door.

4-12.tools: Uses the Extension Cord (0-B) and Cell-Smith.
4-12.music: Every world's theme in turn, climbing toward the Crown.
4-12.visuals: A climbing course of cell-shaped platforms up the Spire's top, a gold cord extending from platform to platform, the Crown's violet glow above.

castle.site: The Null Crown — the top of the Spire, where Null has thrown away every k-invariant and is collapsing the whole Winding Way to a point.
castle.story: Null argues that the homotopy groups are enough and the twists can be thrown away. Gyroid uses every tool he has collected to rebuild the tower stage by stage, putting back each k-invariant. The collapse stops, and every hole returns.
castle.objective: Rebuild the Crown's tower and stop the collapse.

phases.name: The first floor
phases.description: Null's Crown flattens loops into homology; use the Hurewicz needle to restore the first nonzero group. Tests 4-6.

phases.name: The Hopf storm
phases.description: Null hurls linked circles; prove the Hopf map essential to shatter his shield. Tests 4-7.

phases.name: The twists
phases.description: Install the k-invariants Null discarded, stage by stage. Tests 4-11.

phases.name: The summit
phases.description: Extend the restoring map over the last cells; every obstruction class is zero once the twists are in place. Tests 4-12.

phases.name: The ring
phases.description: Echo of World 0: the Ringed Isle returns, hole and all.

enemies.name: The Commutator
enemies.description: Appears in phase 2 and turns on Null.

castle.tools: Every tool: Lash, Spool, Tide Glass, Winding Cord, Clasp, Sheet Compass, Boundary Blade, Degree Dial, Cup Caster, Sling, Extension Cord.
castle.music: Null's theme on full organ, with every world's theme answering it in turn; the World 0 reef theme returns in the final phase.
castle.visuals: A colossal violet crown at the top of the Spire above the clouds, its points collapsing toward a single dark dot; gold brackets reinstalled one by one.
castle.movie: castle-4-intro “The Null Crown” and castle-4-outro / ending “The Crown Unwound”.

4-1.scene: Level 'Cube Root' in Cube Hall: a stone hall filled with glowing cubes whose faces fold toward a single bright gold point; in the center two small glowing subcubes slide past each other. Gyroid stands among the cubes. A violet cube sentry hovers.

4-2.scene: Level 'Snap to Grid' in the Grid Gallery: a gallery hall whose every surface carries glowing grid lines; a gold line snaps onto the grid; a glowing circle slips off a large sphere sculpture. Gyroid walks the gallery. A violet static sprite crackles.

4-3.scene: Level 'Weak Spot': two identical-looking rooms facing each other across a stone floor in a tall tower, small gold courier figures running between them. Gyroid stands in the middle, looking from one to the other.

4-4.scene: Level 'Suspension of Disbelief' at Sling Landing: a balcony over a vast vertical shaft inside a stone tower; Gyroid is slung upward inside a glowing gold double-cone of light; glowing spheres are stacked up the shaft.

4-5.scene: Level 'One Group Per Floor': stacked floors inside a stone tower, each lit by a single color; Gyroid attaches glowing gold cells to fill openings in the ceiling above.

4-6.scene: Level 'Hurewicz Hurrah' in Hurewicz Hall: a hall with two great instruments side by side — a brass dial and a glowing abacus — joined by a gold needle. Gyroid reads them. Emmy Boundary takes notes.

4-7.scene: Level 'Hop Off' at the Hopf Ring: a tower floor encircled by many glowing gold circles, every one linked through every other like the Hopf fibration, forming a nested torus pattern; a small sphere island floats beneath. Gyroid stands at the center. A violet wraith slips between the circles.

4-8.scene: Level 'Stable Ground': a calm stone terrace high above the clouds on a tower; a wall chart of glowing beads (no text). Gyroid and Emmy Boundary rest, looking out.

4-9.scene: Level 'Maps Are Classes' in the Classing Room: lantern beams bend into gold rails that lead up to a single-colored floor above. Gyroid follows a rail with a gold chalice.

4-10.scene: Level 'Fibration Station': a station inside the tower with layered tracks, trains on the upper tracks shadowing every move of trains on lower tracks. Gyroid on a platform with a glowing compass. Violet sprites ride the upper tracks.

4-11.scene: Level 'A Twist in the Tower': stacked tower floors joined by twisted glowing gold brackets; violet hands pry at one bracket. Gyroid lashes the hands away.

4-12.scene: Level 'Obstruction Course': a climbing course of cube- and disk-shaped platforms up the very top of a stone tower, a gold cord extending from platform to platform; a violet crown's glow above in the clouds. Gyroid climbs.

castle_art.scene: Castle 'The Null Crown': a colossal violet crown structure at the top of a tower above the clouds, its points bending inward toward a single dark dot. Count Null (from the reference) stands at the center, arms raised. Gyroid faces him with a gold lasso, gold brackets of light orbiting him; Emmy Boundary beside him; the Commutator stands apart, turning toward Null.

videos.title: Up the Postnikov Spire
videos.plays: After castle-3 (The Counterfeit Station), before World 4 · Level 1
videos.synopsis: Unmasked by a nonzero cup product, the Commutator's station falls and Null retreats up his tower into higher homotopy. The ascent: rooms that unfold into higher dimensions, the Null Crown waiting at the top. Null's final claim: give him the homotopy groups and he can rebuild any space — the twists don't matter.

captions.speaker: Narrator
captions.text: The last province was not land at all, but a tower — and every floor had more dimensions than the last.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Up here, loops become spheres. Holes of every dimension, wrapping each other.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: He's pulling the whole Winding Way in. Everything we restored.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: Give me the groups and I'll rebuild any space. These twists? Ornament.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Those twists hold the tower together. Let's go up and prove it.

videos.synopsis: The first nonzero homotopy group equals the first nonzero homology group.

scenes.title: Two meters
scenes.description: The dial and the abacus side by side.

scenes.title: The needle
scenes.description: A gold needle links them; both read the same.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 20: “World 4 · Level 6 — Hurewicz Hurrah”.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Homotopy on one meter, homology on the other.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: At the first floor where anything happens, they agree. In dimension one, up to order.

videos.title: Hop Off
videos.plays: Before World 4 · Level 7, at the Hopf Ring
videos.synopsis: Null claimed every map S³ → S² is trivial. The Hopf Ring — circles over a sphere, every pair linked — proves him wrong.

scenes.title: The Ring
scenes.description: Linked gold circles encircle the floor.

scenes.title: A circle per point
scenes.description: Gyroid touches points of a small sphere; a circle lights above each.

scenes.title: Linked
scenes.description: Two lit circles pass through each other exactly once.

scenes.title: Null
scenes.description: Null's image flickers, angry.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 30: “World 4 · Level 7 — Hop Off”.

captions.speaker: Narrator
captions.text: Around this floor ran a ring of circles, every one linked through every other.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: A whole circle above each point of the sphere. Together they make a three-sphere.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: And every two circles link. You can't pull that apart.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: So the map from three-sphere to sphere isn't trivial. Null's claim falls.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: One map. A curiosity.

videos.title: Stable Ground
videos.synopsis: Suspend enough and sphere groups settle: the stable stems.

scenes.title: Above the clouds
scenes.description: A calm terrace; the chart wall glows.

scenes.title: Rest
scenes.description: Gyroid and Emmy sit for a moment.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 18: “World 4 · Level 8 — Stable Ground”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Up here nothing changes when you suspend. The numbers settle.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: First calm place in four worlds.

videos.title: Maps Are Classes
videos.synopsis: A reading is the same as a map into a One-Group Floor.

scenes.title: Beams bend
scenes.description: Lantern beams bend into rails leading upward.

scenes.title: Up the rail
scenes.description: Gyroid follows a rail to a single-colored floor.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 18: “World 4 · Level 9 — Maps Are Classes”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Every reading from the Gardens is a map into one of these floors.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Lanterns were maps all along.

videos.title: Fibration Station
videos.synopsis: Covers lifted paths; fibrations lift every deformation.

scenes.title: Layered tracks
scenes.description: Trains on upper tracks shadow every lower train.

scenes.title: Lift
scenes.description: A lower train swerves; its upper twin swerves in step.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 20: “World 4 · Level 10 — Fibration Station”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The Sheetwater Viaduct lifted paths. This station lifts any deformation.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Whatever moves down there, something up here moves with it.

videos.title: A Twist in the Tower
videos.plays: Before World 4 · Level 11, on the Twist
videos.synopsis: Every place is a tower of one-group floors joined by twists. Same floors, different twists: different places.

scenes.title: Brackets
scenes.description: Twisted gold brackets join the floors.

scenes.title: Untwist
scenes.description: Emmy removes a bracket's twist; the floor above changes shape.

scenes.title: Thieves
scenes.description: Violet hands reach for the brackets.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 26: “World 4 · Level 11 — A Twist in the Tower”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Each floor holds one group. The twists between them hold the place together.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Same floors, no twist — and it's a different tower.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: That's what Null threw away. He's going to get it wrong.

videos.title: Obstruction Course
videos.synopsis: Extend a map cell by cell to the summit; each blockage is a cohomology class.

scenes.title: The course
scenes.description: Cell-shaped platforms climb toward the Crown.

scenes.title: Extension Cord
scenes.description: Gyroid unspools the Extension Cord from World 0, platform to platform.

scenes.title: Blocked
scenes.description: A platform refuses the cord; a violet class glows on it.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 24: “World 4 · Level 12 — Obstruction Course”.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: The Extension Cord. Feels like years since the Cylinder Works.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Extend over each cell. When a cell blocks you, the block is a reading.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Then I change what's below and try again.

videos.title: The Null Crown
videos.synopsis: At the top of the Spire, Null is collapsing the Winding Way. The Commutator arrives — and stands with Gyroid.

scenes.title: The summit
scenes.description: The Crown pulses; through it the Winding Way contracts below.

scenes.title: Null
scenes.description: Null turns, Crown blazing, brackets falling away around him.

scenes.title: An ally
scenes.description: The Commutator steps out of a violet ribbon beside Gyroid and lowers his blade toward Null.

scenes.title: Ready
scenes.description: Gyroid's tools glow at once.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 32: “World 4 · Castle — The Null Crown”.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: Every hole you saved, courier. I'm folding them all to a point.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: You threw away the twists. Your tower can't stand.

captions.speaker: The Commutator
captions.text: Order matters, Null. So does structure. I won't be folded.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Every tool, Gyroid. Every world.

videos.title: The Crown Unwound
videos.plays: After castle-4 (The Null Crown) — the game is won
videos.synopsis: Gyroid rebuilds the Crown's tower stage by stage, installing the k-invariants Null threw away, and disconnects its collapse drive. The ringed island returns — hole and all — and every province is restored without erasing a single hole. Callback to the opening: shape changed, topology didn't. Null is not destroyed but reshaped, and Emmy's last line names the theme. Credits carry Hatcher's Algebraic Topology attribution.

scenes.title: Rebuilt
scenes.description: The last gold bracket clicks into place; the Crown's points straighten; its collapse drive gutters out.

scenes.title: Null, reshaped
scenes.description: Null's cloak unravels into a ring of violet light around him; he is smaller, unmasked, holding a small torus in his hands and staring at its hole.

scenes.title: The Way returns
scenes.description: From the Spire's top, the camera sweeps down over every province expanding back: Retract Reef, Bouquet Bastion's two districts, Chain Delta's empty middle, the Gardens' lanterns, the Reach's seam.

scenes.title: The Ringed Isle
scenes.description: Back at Retract Reef: the Ringed Isle rises from the sea, hole and all, exactly as in the opening — but now Callimachus's library lanterns line its rim. Gyroid, Emmy and the Commutator stand on it.

scenes.title: Last line
scenes.description: Gyroid coils his lasso into a loop around his arm; Emmy looks out at the restored Way.

scenes.title: Credits
scenes.description: Title card at 52: “Winding World” — “Based on Algebraic Topology by Allen Hatcher (Cambridge University Press, 2002)”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Every twist back where it belongs. The tower stands.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: I only wanted it simple. A point is so… simple.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Keep the torus. Look at its hole for a while. It's not going anywhere.

captions.speaker: Narrator
captions.text: The Winding Way unrolled, province by province — every shape a little different, every hole exactly where it had been.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: The ring's back. Same hole. We never had to erase anything.

captions.speaker: The Commutator
captions.text: In order, I hope.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Shapes change, Gyroid. What can't be undone is what makes them themselves.
